segments.text: There is exactly one food in the Qur'an that Allah calls a healing. Not a blessing... not a provision. A healing. And it comes out of the body of an insect.
segments._shot: golden honey pouring in slow motion, backlit

segments.text: This is the verse... of the honey.
segments.title: THE HONEY
segments.titleSub: a healing named in the Qur'an
segments._shot: slow amber light refracting on black

segments.text: The sixteenth chapter of the Qur'an is named an-Nahl... The Bee. In it, Allah describes inspiring the bee to build homes in the mountains and trees, to feed from every fruit... and then to produce something that was never for the bee alone.
segments._shot: bees working wildflowers in golden light

segments.text: There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors... in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign... for a people who give thought.

And the Prophet, peace be upon him, staked a cure on that verse. A man came to him saying... my brother's stomach is ailing. He said... give him honey. The man came back... it grew worse. Again... honey. Until the Prophet said... Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied. He drank it... and he was cured.
segments._shot: tea-colored honey stirred into a glass cup, steam

segments.text: The verse says healing for people... it never said every disease, and Muslims do not read it as a replacement for medicine. But fourteen centuries later, honey sits in modern wound clinics and pharmacology journals... the pantry food found still edible in tombs thousands of years old... still earning its verse.
segments._shot: jars of honey in warm window light

segments.text: Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought. The bee cannot know what it makes. The question the chapter asks is quieter... do you know who taught it?
segments._shot: a bee lifting off a flower into soft light
